stories.title: FAA lifts nationwide US ground stop after telecom failure; thousands of flights cancelled
stories.summary: The FAA halted flights across the United States at 3:54pm ET on Friday, 13 November, after a telecommunications outage hit air route traffic control centres; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the airspace reopened at 8:15pm ET. Duffy said overloaded switches and routers failed, and officials said new technology added to the system overloaded older components, while Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said no cyberattack was linked. FlightRadar24 counted more than 4,700 cancellations and 10,000 delays on Friday, with about 700 flights already cancelled for Saturday. Duffy warned it would take time to get back to full capacity.

stories.title: S&P 500 and Nasdaq slip Friday as 10-year Treasury yield closes near 5.15%
stories.summary: The S&P 500 fell 0.40% to 7,561.67 and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 0.91% to 25,136.27 on Friday, while the Dow rose 0.10% to 52,347.55; all three still posted weekly gains. October producer prices rose 0.3% month over month, below the 0.4% expected, but 6.5% year over year, the largest annual increase since November 2022, keeping pressure on the Fed to raise rates next month. The 10-year Treasury yield closed at about 5.15% after touching 5.17%. Nvidia fell 2% to $162.85, leaving its market value below $4 trillion ahead of earnings due Tuesday.

stories.title: Senate Banking Committee summons ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Lutnick
stories.summary: Senate Banking Committee chair Tim Scott asked former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to appear at a public hearing on 3 December, threatening subpoenas if they refuse. Three House committees separately asked Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter to appear on 1 and 2 December. Huang resigned on 12 November amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman US authorities suspect of spying for China, which China denies. Lawmakers are also examining whether Nvidia's advanced chip exports to China received proper scrutiny.

stories.title: Qatar and Turkiye sign mutual defence pact in Istanbul
stories.summary: Qatar and Turkiye agreed to take a common position against external armed attacks targeting either country, following a Supreme Strategic Committee meeting in Istanbul on 13 November chaired by President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani. The pact also expands consultation on security threats, joint military exercises, defence industry collaboration and training exchanges, though the communique does not say what would trigger a joint response. It comes amid the US-Israeli war on Iran and disruption to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, and both countries called for unimpeded passage through the strait.

stories.title: Canada and the Philippines conclude free-trade negotiations, aim to sign in 2027
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. formally ended negotiations on a bilateral free-trade agreement in Manila, on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit, with signing expected next year. Ottawa first began exploring a deal with the Philippines in 2015, and Carney rebooted the talks just over a year ago. Businesses broadly supported the deal during consultations, while civil society groups raised concerns about the Philippines' record on environment, labour and human rights. Canada is also pursuing a wider trade agreement with ASEAN as it seeks to diversify trade.

stories.title: COP31 reaches midpoint in Antalya with limited progress on key texts
stories.summary: Climate talks at COP31 in Antalya, co-presided by Turkiye and Australia, reached their sixth day with a stocktaking plenary expected to reveal countries' first red lines. Some large developing countries have objected to sectoral targets such as a voluntary pledge to raise electrification to 35% by 2035, and the draft cover text is still a list of every tabled proposal. African countries are prioritising a tripling of adaptation finance to at least $120 billion a year by 2035. UN climate chief Simon Stiell described progress as constructive.
